Most of the recent feedback is on [merge request !3](https://gitlab.lrz.de/hephaestustest/introcourse/heph-lifecycle-e2e-20260927/session-resume-procedure/-/merge_requests/3) — five *not met* practices, all from the finished review last Monday:

- **Insecure file access** — request query feeds straight into `contentRoot.resolve`, so the handler can read files outside the content directory.
- **Unvalidated input** — unbounded query; missing files still return 200.
- **Swallowed error** — the missing-file `IOException` is absorbed into an always-200 response.
- **No covering test** — the new handler ships with nothing to lock it in.
- **No recorded rationale** — the new endpoint ships without a note on why.

The one that matters most is the **insecure file access**. It's the only one that's a security exposure rather than a correctness gap — a crafted query can pull files out of the directory your own javadoc says is the boundary. The other three (validation, error handling, test) are all downstream of the same root: the query is treated as trusted. Fix that containment check first and half the rest follows.
